proposal.name: Check acceptance sources against the decision graph

plan.name: Check acceptance sources against the decision graph
plan.summary: Before proposing a built-in Go plumbing plan for a repository with decisions/journal, use the existing journal rebuild and graph check on the base copy after all acceptance sources have been staged, with a fresh temporary store. Return journal rebuild failures and every graph problem as draft feedback through Checked.Problem and Feedback, so both the planner's check tool and the factory's final proposal check refuse the draft with the checker's diagnostics, without changing the original checkout or the machine's decision store. Preserve the existing acceptance failure-evidence rules and behavior without a journal; recorded decision mentions and fixture IDs assembled at run time remain eligible when their acceptance tests fail. Update SPEC.md and docs/factory.md to describe this additional check, citing the recorded decision-graph and plumbing-plan foundations. Whoever merges records the new decision extending those foundations, since this plumbing build cannot write decisions/.

tests.name: TestPlanCheckReportsAcceptanceDecisionGraphProblems
tests.says: The plan check refuses unknown decision mentions in every staged acceptance source with the graph check's diagnostics, permits correction to recorded or runtime-built IDs, preserves checks without a journal and rejection of already-passing tests, and leaves the base and draft unchanged.

tests.name: TestPlanCheckUsesTheExistingJournalAndGraphValidation
tests.says: Checking the staged copy also refuses malformed journals and the existing graph check's SPEC and journal-log problems, reporting their diagnostics as draft problems.

tests.name: TestPlanProposalRequiresValidAcceptanceDecisionGraph
tests.says: The factory's final planning check refuses an unchecked draft with an unknown acceptance citation before creating a proposal, while recorded citations and runtime-built fixture IDs still produce proposals with their exact plan and sources.

usage.summary: Wrote `plan.json` and three acceptance tests covering decision-graph validation before proposal, with documentation updates. The first check passed: all three tests fail against the unchanged base, as required.
